messages.subject: Re: Null model used in the M2 function
parts:
On Wed, Apr 12, 2017 at 1:09 AM, Zhang, Bo <bozh...@illinois.edu> wrote:

Hi Phil,

 

I was just wondering what's the null model for computing the CFI/TLI in the M2 function ?

It's an intercept only model, with K-1 intercepts for each response category in the items.
 

Also, do you have any idea how reliable are these M2-based model fit indexes compared to those computed in the SEM framework?

I'm sure people have studied this in the literature.
 

Are we also able to get fit indexes that are based on ordinary chi-square in mirt. 

Yes, but only for dense response tables (which only occurs when the number of items is small).
 

In my case, the performance of TLI and CFI is kind of weird. I even get CFI of 0 and TLI of -0.5. It's really hard to imagine. So I guess it has something to do with the null model. Any idea on this?

 

If the performance of TLI/CFI has not been validated, what can I use to do model comparisons in addition to chisquare, AIC and BIC?

In mirt, nothing else at the moment.
 

 

 

Best,

Bo
